title: Getting Started
description: Get an overview of the workshop, the concepts it covers, and the multi-agent travel planning use case you will build

title: [Hands-on] Launch Solace Agent Mesh
description: Launch Solace Agent Mesh in a GitHub Codespace, or install and configure SAM Desktop on your machine

title: The Agent Development Lifecycle
description: Understand why agents need their own lifecycle and the five stages of the ADLC: Build, Test, Deploy, Observe, and Improve

title: What is Solace Agent Mesh
description: Understand the Solace Agent Mesh architecture, why it is built on an event broker, Quick Build, and its components: agents, tools, connectors, and entrypoints

title: Declarative SAM and the CLI
description: Learn the sam CLI and declarative configuration: config repositories, manifests, plan and apply, secrets, targets, and AI-assisted authoring

title: [Hands-on] Using Built-in Tools
description: Build general-purpose agents that use built-in tools with Quick Build, and have the orchestrator use them together

title: [Hands-on] Using Custom Tools
description: Add the travel-planner custom Go toolset with sam config apply, or package it and upload it through the web UI

title: [Hands-on] Connectors
description: Connect to the flights and hotels databases and the Places MCP server

title: [Hands-on] Agents
description: Create the flight, hotel, local experiences, and travel orchestrator agents

title: [Hands-on] A2A Proxy
description: Connect the external LangChain weather advisor agent to the mesh through an A2A proxy

title: [Hands-on] Run the System
description: Test each agent on its own, then plan a full trip through the travel orchestrator
